chrome_playback.clip_and_cut_playback: Close take (8s), first camera cut (2s), second camera cut (2s), and final 14s export completed in Chrome. Temporal samples and exact endings also reviewed.

findings: Fresh clean starts did not reproduce the earlier spreading airborne dots in the reviewed half-second temporal samples. This short test does not prove their elimination or absence between samples.

Four of five complete takes were rejected. Resting and deep-breath actions opened the mouth; deep-breath takes changed the coat, torso or markings. A selected mouth correction did not reliably fix the problem.
The close window-looking clip was the only full eight-second take accepted for this draft. Gills/neck and props remained visually coherent in its samples; final user creative review is still pending.

The final 14-second sample is an editorial salvage: 4s from the first wide take, the full 8s close take, and 2s from the settled ending of the first deep-breath take. It does not demonstrate a successful deep breath or the original 24-second plan.

The same clean exterior reappears on fresh starts. Camera cuts mask some pose differences but do not establish a continuously progressing panorama. The final wide tail is more extended and the eyes close at the cut.

App service import supports an explicit source frame range; the normal UI lacks that selection. A review-time start change was correctly refused; a separate range import created the correct packet. The source player still displays the full native source while review samples/join/export use the imported range.

The current selected correction template omits much of the recorded failure detail. After a mouth correction it does not also constrain unwanted hand or coat motion. Calm action control needs further qualification rather than repeated blind generation.

The app runs persisted prompts, bounded retries, authenticated imports, reviewed cut packets and exact export. Custom short recipes and source-range selection in this test used its existing authenticated API. No per-video FFmpeg repair, retiming, loops or padding were used.

Generation and image preparation remain assistant-operated in the Flow UI. Native Save dialogs require handling; one downloadMedia call stalled about 16 minutes. Monthly human effort, 30 videos/month and unattended control remain unqualified.
